lines.speaker: F
lines.text: The Rhine at Kaub read thirteen centimetres over the weekend, and barges need about seventy-seven for a full channel.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: The bottleneck is getting worse, not easing. This is The Planning Desk.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Good morning, it's Monday the ninth of November, and I'm Anna.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Quick note, this show is made with A I. A I agents gather the news, and our voices are synthetic.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: The Kaub gauge on the Rhine read thirteen centimetres at lunchtime on Sunday, down from nineteen on Saturday, according to the federal Pegelonline gauges.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Barges need roughly seventy-seven centimetres at Kaub for a shipping channel of one metre ninety, so the river is a long way short.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Further down, Emmerich on the Dutch border read minus two centimetres over the weekend, Köln sixty-three and Duisburg-Ruhrort one hundred and fifty-one.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: We have more data than ever, and most forecasts aren't getting much better, because more data also means more noise to mistake for a pattern.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The forecasters who do improve share a few plain habits, and planners can copy every one of them.
